1.1.handover:
# Handover 1.1 — Keep moving troops inside their validated domain

**What landed**

`872b437 Keep troop movement inside the interior` restricts distance-field
traversal and troop destinations to `x=1..238, y=1..158`. An interior source
seeds distance zero; a boundary cursor seeds its cardinal interior neighbours at
distance one; a corner cursor leaves the hostile field with no reachable interior
cells, so enemies wait. Additions to `tests/core/survival-waves.test.ts` cover the
exact `(5,0)` / `(4,1)` case moving east to `(5,1)` with a snapshot round-trip,
all four edges, all four corners, and partition invariance with occupancy.
`tests/core/survival-allies.test.ts` covers allies advancing to a top-edge rally
while the cursor sits on the boundary. `docs/survival-coverage.md` records the
interior-only contract and the new regression examples.

**Landmark drift**

The plan's `inWorld` and movement line numbers have shifted by roughly 10 lines
after the helper and test additions. `distanceField` is now near
`src/core/world.ts:1276`; the ally/hostile candidate checks are near 1338 and
1371. The plan's `inWorld` landmark still exists but is now only used to reject
sources outside the world; interior checks use the new `inInterior` helper.

**Deviations from the work order**

No public interface changed. I added one private `inInterior(x, y)` helper and
used it in the existing interior validators (`troopPosition`, `rallyCell`,
`rallyProblem`, `insideInterior`) to keep their behavior identical and their
domain consistent. The plan only required movement and BFS changes; this reuse
is behavior-preserving. I added the ally boundary example as a second movement
suite example.

**What the next session must know**

- Cursor navigation still reaches every boundary cell and is untouched.
- Boundary sources generally are virtual sources, but rally and enemy sources
  are already validated interior cells, so in practice only the cursor can be a
  boundary source.
- Corner cursors produce an all-`-1` hostile field; the existing `<= 0` wait
  check keeps enemies still. Adjacent-enemy and adjacent-cursor combat holds are
  unchanged.
- `direnv exec . just verify` passed: 292 core tests, 106 browser tests across
  both projects, typecheck, contract checks, first-playable completion and
  benchpress lint. No flake change, so `just check-nix` was not run.

**Open problems**

None.

# Handover 1.2 — Enforce living population caps in survival scenarios

**What landed**

`9994896 Reject over-cap living troops in survival scenarios` makes
`parseTroops` count supplied allies by origin ring and enemies as it parses.
More than `IMP_CAP` living allies for one ring or more than `ENEMY_CAP` living
enemies now rejects scenario construction; supplied troops are never trimmed.
Exactly-at-cap setups, five allies from each of multiple rings, and a
million-produced ring with five living allies are accepted and round-trip.
`tests/core/survival-combat.test.ts` and `tests/core/survival-waves.test.ts`
hold the new regression examples; `docs/survival-coverage.md` records them and
the construction-time cap contract.

**Landmark drift**

The work order's `src/core/world.ts:710` still points at `parseTroops`; the
population counters added eight lines, so guards and later movement code shifted
slightly. `survivalTroopSetup` is unchanged. Production and wave guards remain
at their previous locations and were not modified.

**Deviations from the work order**

None functionally. The enemy regression uses the work order's `(20+i,20)` cells
and IDs `n0..n128`; the ally large-produced example uses the existing `ring`
helper with `produced: 1_000_000`. Checks count while parsing rather than in a
second pass, so an over-cap list fails at the offending troop with a descriptive
message. No public interface changed.

**What the next session must know**

- Validation is per origin ring, not per position or `produced`; serials still
  only need to be positive and not exceed `produced`.
- The legacy five-produced cap in `buildingSetup` remains separate and intact.
- `direnv exec . just verify` and `direnv exec . just test` both passed:
  294 core tests, 106 browser tests across both projects, typecheck, contract
  checks, first-playable completion and benchpress lint. No flake change, so
  `just check-nix` was not run.
- The worktree is clean after the commit.

# Handover 1.3 — Keep navigation-only worlds free of survival simulation

**What landed**

`6b980ab Keep navigation-only worlds out of survival simulation` makes
`tickWorld` return after incrementing `elapsedTicks` whenever `navigationOnly`
is set. Economy, wave spawning, troop movement and combat no longer run for
navigation-only worlds of either rules profile, while `advance` still owns
remainder arithmetic, pause and hidden suspension.

`tests/core/survival-profile.test.ts` advances a navigation-only survival world
by 105000 ms in one call and through `[1, 99, 100, 300, 600, 500, 900, 12500,
20000, 70000]`, crossing four wave boundaries. It asserts equal observations and
snapshots across partitions, zero troops/wave/next-wave, preserved custom rows
and `w` motion, snapshot round-trip plus future advancement, exact 250 ms clock
arithmetic, paused/hidden clocks, and an ordinary survival wave-1 control.
`docs/survival-coverage.md` records the revision; no public interface changed.

**Landmark drift**

The work order's `tickWorld` at `src/core/world.ts:1456` is now at 1468; the
body is otherwise the same. The new guard is at 1470. `parseScenario`,
`compose`, `snapshot` and `observe` landmarks moved with earlier unit changes
but retain their navigation-only branches and were not edited.

**Deviations from the work order**

The guard skips all tick simulation for every navigation-only profile, not only
survival. This matches the unit's navigation-only contract, is unobservable for
the historical profile (its snapshot and observations already omit buildings),
and avoids hidden legacy economy inside a navigation fixture. No test was
deleted or weakened.

**What the next session must know**

- `advance` still handles remainder partitions, tick overflow, pause and
  suspension before `tickWorld`; the guard only suppresses simulation phases.
- Navigation-only observations already hard-code `wave: 0` and
  `nextWaveTick: 0`; the fix also guarantees `troops` is genuinely empty.
- `direnv exec . just test` passed 295 core tests. `direnv exec . just verify`
  passed both browser projects (106 tests), typecheck, contract checks,
  first-playable completion and benchpress lint. No flake change, so
  `just check-nix` was not run.
- The worktree is clean after the commit.

**Open problems**

None.

commits: b1e6f746e655e173192cfbb743f16f989a4bba48 Reject survival counter overflow before returning a world
1.4.handover:
# Handover 1.4 — Preserve the numeric domain across survival transitions

**What landed**

`b1e6f74 Reject survival counter overflow before returning a world` adds a
private `checkedCounter(value, increment, label)` helper in `src/core/world.ts`
and applies it to every survival counter increment named by the work order:
production serial allocation, ally and enemy spawn cooldowns, combat and cursor
damage cooldowns, input-contact cooldown, and kill accumulation. The helper
throws `Invalid world scenario: <label> exceeds the safe integer domain` before
`advance` or `dispatch` constructs a world, so the supplied world is unchanged.

`tests/core/survival-combat.test.ts` reproduces funded production at
`produced:Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, kill accumulation at `kills:MAX` and combat
cooldown overflow at `elapsedTicks:MAX-1`; each throws without changing the
world's snapshot or observation. It also checks the last representable serial,
kill and cooldown round-trip through `game.scenario(game.snapshot(world))`, plus
idle and blocked rings at maximum production.
`tests/core/survival-waves.test.ts` covers input-contact overflow and the last
representable contact cooldown, and a wave spawned at the last representable wave
tick with exact spawn cooldowns. `docs/survival-coverage.md` records the error
boundary.

**Landmark drift**

The work order's line numbers had drifted with units 1.2/1.3: production serial
is now `world.ts:1207`, spawn cooldowns at 1217/1455, combat cooldowns at
1248/1251, kill accumulation at 1496, and input contact at 1905. The transition
bodies themselves matched the plan. `advance`'s elapsed-tick guard remains at
1515. The plan's `produced:M` example overflow value was one off (`M` is
`...991`; `M+1` is not safe); the tests use the actual domain boundary.

**Deviations from the work order**

No behavioral deviation. The wave spawn cooldown guard is defensive: with wave
ticks at `300 + 200k`, the largest in-domain wave tick is `MAX-91`, so its
cooldown is `MAX-81`; the overflow branch is not reachable through normal wave
timing but is checked for consistency. No test was deleted or weakened.

**What the next session must know**

- `checkedCounter` is private and uses the same `fail` prefix as `advance`'s
  elapsed-tick overflow, so runtime errors read `Invalid world scenario: ...`.
- Checks run before the world is constructed; in multi-tick `advance` calls an
  overflow on any intermediate tick throws and leaves the original input intact.
- Idle and blocked transitions at maximum counters remain valid and round-trip.
- `direnv exec . just test` passed 300 core tests; `direnv exec . just verify`
  passed the 106 browser tests, typecheck, contract checks, first-playable
  completion and benchpress lint. No flake change, so `just check-nix` was not
  run.
- The worktree is clean after the commit.

**Open problems**

None.

commits: 9f47d6348362657ed8a99ba647eac11164341310 Keep survival prompts and status readable
1.5.handover:
# Handover 1.5 — Make survival prompts and status actually readable

**What landed**

`9f47d63 Keep survival prompts and status readable` adds a presentation-only
survival overlay in `index.html` and `src/web/style.css`: `#survival-prompt`
carries the current Insert/Name/Finder/Build label, help text and notice;
`#survival-status` carries HP/nearby health, wave/countdown, kills, population,
rally coordinates, staged source, time/pause state, the faction legend and the
`i rally Enter` hint. `src/web/main.ts` fills both overlays from the same values
as the HUD and sets `body[data-rules]`, so the overlay appears only in survival.
The overlay is absolutely positioned above the unchanged 32-pixel HUD, wraps
long text and has `pointer-events: none`; it does not alter world geometry,
core rules, keyboard handling or the legacy layout.

`tests/browser/survival-readability.spec.ts` adds eight real-key cases (four
sizes in both projects). Each checks initial status, paused/running time,
Insert candidates/draft, an unknown-command notice, a 20-character Name draft
with its default/commit/cancel prompt, the committed long name, a staged `b001`
source, connect/rally candidates at a ring, and nearby ally health. It asserts
panel rectangles and wrapped scroll dimensions fit inside the viewport and that
the document does not scroll.

**Landmark drift**

The work order's evidence line numbers were still close: HUD remains
`src/web/style.css:44`-ish and the old 720px media query follows the new overlay
rules. `describeSite`/`render` in `src/web/main.ts` are now around lines 127 and
490; the HUD update block is near line 588. No core landmarks moved.

**Deviations from the work order**

No behavioral deviation from D3. The HUD elements stay populated as before for
existing tests and the legacy profile; the overlays are additive rather than a
replacement. The overlay shows a long building name whenever the cursor is on a
building even in Normal mode, matching the done-when's long-name requirement.
`README.md` and `docs/direction.md` received one sentence each to keep their
description of the readable presentation current; `docs/survival-coverage.md`
records the new DOM elements, regression suite and unchanged core interface.

**What the next session must know**

- The prompt panel is hidden when the mode is Normal, the cursor is not on a
  site, and there is no notice. Notice text is rendered only while the prompt
  panel is visible.
- Status text is duplicated deliberately: `#hud-*` remains for legacy checks and
  the historical layout; `#survival-*` is the readable survival surface.
- The overlay is `position: absolute` inside `#game`, starts at `left: 56px`
  (after the gutter) and sits at `bottom: 40px`, so it never changes canvas
  dimensions.
- Browser wave label starts at `wave 0` because `nextWaveTick` is 300; the first
  spawned wave is 1. Do not expect `wave 1` before tick 300.
- `direnv exec . just verify` passed: 300 core tests, 114 browser tests in both
  projects, first-playable completion, contract checks, typecheck and benchpress
  lint. `direnv exec . just test` also passed. No flake change, so
  `just check-nix` was not run.
- The worktree is clean after the commit.

**Open problems**

None.
